newsitem.title: USA: Johnson Q1 global drug sales rise 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Q1 global drug sales rise 10.3 pct.

text.p: Johnson & Johnson said Tuesday its global pharmaceutical sales rose by 10.3 percent to $1.9 billion in the first quarter from the year ago period despite the impact of a strong dollar.

"Of particular note was the strength of our domestic pharmaceutical business and the impressive growth of all business in the Asia-Pacific region," Ralph Larsen, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Although the strength of the dollar had a significant negative impact on its international sales, Larsen said the company was pleased with its top line growth on a local currency basis.

Larson said he was pleased with the continuing strong performance of Johnson & Johnson. However, the impact of the strong dollar relative to foreign currencies still decreased first quarter sales by 3.1 percent.
Worldwide consumer segment sales rose by four percent over the same period a year ago led by continued strength in the hair and skin care franchise, the company said.

First quarter professional segment global sales rose 6.9 percent to $2.1 billion led by a strong performance in such areas including contact lenses, invasive surgical instruments and blood glucose monitoring systems.
Johnson & Johnson, based in New Brunswick, N.J., is a comprehensive manufacturer of health care products serving consumer, pharmaceutical, diagnostics and professional markets.
